name: Aging & Disability Resource LINK (North Dakota Health and Human Services)
organization: Aging & Disability Resource LINK (North Dakota Health and Human Services)
description: The Aging & Disability Resource LINK, run statewide by North Dakota Health and Human Services: free information and referral on help at home, meals, caregiver support, assisted living and other long-term services for older adults, adults with disabilities and caregivers, at any income.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. Press 1 for the Resource LINK. TTY users can call 711. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
Statewide; one number for all 53 counties. Press 1 for the Resource LINK.

source_evidence.title: North Dakota Health and Human Services: Adults and Aging Services
source_evidence.scope: Aging and Disability Resource LINK, toll-free (855) 462-5465, Relay ND TTY 711; the Adults and Aging Services section, 1237 W. Divide Avenue, Suite 6, Bismarck; read in full. The page is undated. The 2023 Vulnerable Adult Protective Services handout gives option 1 for the Resource LINK (https://www.hhs.nd.gov/sites/www/files/documents/vaps-handout-2023.pdf; search excerpt). North Dakota has no Area Agencies on Aging; the state section runs Older Americans Act services statewide.

name: North Dakota State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
organization: North Dakota State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: North Dakota Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program brochure (DN 647, December 2023)
source_evidence.scope: State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Adult and Aging Services, 1237 W. Divide Ave., Suite 6, Bismarck: 701-328-4617 or 711 (TTY), toll-free 1-855-462-5465, option 3; read in full. The brochure lists no regional ombudsmen, so every county shows the state office.
